findings.requirement_type: Cyber Liability — Minimum Limits ($5M Per Occurrence)
findings.gap_description: The Maricopa contract requires $5M PER OCCURRENCE Cyber. The AmTrust Cyber policy carries a $4,000,000 AGGREGATE Limit of Liability shared across all 14 cyber coverage lines (Ransom, Data Recovery, Bricking, BI, BI from Suppliers, Reputation Harm, Cyber Event, Cyber Deception, Proof of Loss, Cryptojacking, Privacy & Network Security, Regulatory Fines, Payment Card, Media). On its face this is $1M short of the contract minimum, AND the structure is fundamentally weaker — a per-occurrence requirement reloads for each event, while a shared aggregate exhausts. The Hanover Umbrella (475-0654 / 475-0655 / 475-0661) expressly excludes cyber, data privacy, and confidential information access/disclosure on BOTH Coverage A and Coverage B, so umbrella drop-down is unavailable. As of policy inception 4/1/2025 this is an uncured contract breach under §8.2.13.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber Liability — Defense Within Limits + Shared Aggregate Erosion
findings.gap_description: On a typical cyber claim, 60-80% of recovery is consumed by forensics, breach counsel, PR, and regulatory defense. With Defense Within Limits on a $4M aggregate that is also SHARED across 14 coverage lines, the effective indemnity available to the insured on a single claim is approximately $800,000 to $1,600,000. This is dramatically below the $5M per-occurrence minimum spirit of the Maricopa contract, and below the realistic exposure for a vendor handling 90M+ voter records across 31 states. There is no excess cyber tower to backstop exhaustion. Hanover Umbrella (475-0654/0655/0661) expressly excludes cyber/data privacy on both Coverage A and Coverage B — no follow-form drop-down available.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber Liability — Social Engineering / Cyber Deception Phantom Coverage
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Hartford Management Liability Crime — but only $15K Deception Fraud sublimit; combined exposure is still phantom
findings.gap_description: The Cyber Deception sublimit is $250,000 with a $250,000 retention — meaning the effective recoverable on any single loss is $0, and on a $500K loss the recovery is capped at $250K (50%). The Hartford Management Liability Crime form provides $15,000 of Deception Fraud / Social Engineering coverage (PP 00 H600 §V(T)) — also de minimis. Combined, the program offers effectively no meaningful protection against social engineering / fraudulent instruction wire-transfer fraud — a top-3 fraud loss category for businesses processing county invoices and vendor payments. This pattern is a classic example of 'phantom coverage' where retention equals limit. Cross-policy mitigation does not materially close the gap — Ugly retained because both available policies are de minimis.

findings.requirement_type: D&O — Manufacturing & Professional Services Exclusion Bars Core Operations
findings.gap_description: Hartford Private Choice Premier Management Liability includes an absolute exclusion barring D&O coverage for any claim arising from product malfunction OR rendering/failure to render services for fees. Run-Test Election Services' ENTIRE BUSINESS is rendering printing, mailing, and ballot processing SERVICES FOR FEES to county clients. The carve-backs (security-holder civil proceedings without management participation, derivative actions/demands) protect against narrow shareholder scenarios but do not protect against the most likely claim: a county or downstream voter suing the company over election-services execution failures. For a PE-backed company where Lincoln Shields LLC and Black Mountain Investment Company LLC have D&O representatives sitting on the cap table, this exclusion eviscerates Side B (corporate indemnification) and Side C (entity coverage) for the company's core operational risks. Tech E&O ($10M tower) will respond to professional services claims against the entity but does NOT provide Side A/B/C protection for individual directors and officers — these are different coverage triggers and do not substitute. No other D&O policy in the program. Truly absolute gap.

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Notice of Cancellation — Maricopa County
findings.policy_file: redacted - Hanover - WC - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf; RedactedHanover - Auto - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf; Redacted2024-26 Management Liability Policy.pdf; RedactedCyber_Assoc Industries.AmTrust_04.25-04.26 #AES123191302.pdf
findings.policy_page: WC p 112; Auto pp 44-46; ML/Cyber/E&O — none
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.15 requires 30-day written notice to Maricopa County on every required policy (GL, Auto, WC, Umbrella, Cyber, E&O). The Hanover WC and Auto NOC schedules do NOT list Maricopa County. The Hartford Management Liability, AmTrust Cyber, Gemini E&O primary, and Convex E&O excess have NO Designated Entity NOC endorsement at all. The Hanover Package (401-1235) does carry a NOC schedule but Maricopa is not listed there either. Maricopa expressly characterizes failure to maintain insurance as a material breach (§8.2.2). Sacramento §VI.A.2 imposes a CONTRACTUAL notification duty on the contractor (not a DE NOC requirement on the policy itself), so Sacramento is satisfied operationally.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber — Additional Insured Status (Maricopa)
findings.policy_page: Dec page Item 8, p 4 (no AI endorsement scheduled)
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.7 expressly carves out Workers' Compensation and Errors and Omissions from the Additional Insured requirement — but does NOT carve out Cyber. Cyber Liability is therefore a required AI line under the contract. The AmTrust Cyber policy contains no AI endorsement. Many cyber forms structurally do not accommodate Additional Insured status because the coverage is first-party-heavy and third-party defense flows to the insured organization. Carrier confirmation is required to determine whether AmTrust will endorse Maricopa as an AI on Cyber, or whether an alternative compliance path (e.g., contractual indemnity satisfaction) is acceptable to Maricopa Risk Management. No other cyber policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber — Waiver of Subrogation (Maricopa)
findings.policy_page: Dec page Item 8, p 4 (no WoS endorsement scheduled)
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.8 carves out only Workers' Compensation and Errors and Omissions from the Waiver of Subrogation requirement — Cyber is therefore a required WoS line. AmTrust Cyber policy excerpt shows no WoS endorsement. If a cyber event were caused or contributed to by Maricopa County's act/omission (e.g., a county-side configuration error allowing data exfiltration), AmTrust could subrogate against the county after paying. The contract requires that subrogation right be waived. As with AI, carrier confirmation is required. No other cyber policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber — Primary & Noncontributory (Maricopa)
findings.policy_page: Dec page Item 8, p 4 (no P&NC endorsement scheduled)
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.4 requires P&NC on all required policies including Cyber. AmTrust Cyber excerpt does not show P&NC endorsement. Less impactful than AI/WoS because Maricopa County is unlikely to maintain its own cyber insurance covering Run-Test's data handling, but technical contract non-compliance. No other cyber policy to provide P&NC.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber — Continuity / Retroactive Date Gap
findings.gap_description: AmTrust Cyber Continuity Date is 04/01/2023, only 2 years before current inception. Runbeck Election Services has 50+ years of continuous operations and has held Maricopa, Sacramento, and Los Angeles County contracts for multiple years. Any cyber incident involving acts/omissions or unauthorized access predating 04/01/2023 — such as a persistent threat actor with access dating back further, or a breach not yet discovered — would not be covered. Maricopa contracts effective prior to 04/01/2023 are particularly exposed to retroactive-date gaps under §8.2.3 which requires retro to PRECEDE the contract effective date. Verification of each contract effective date against the 04/01/2023 retro is required. No other cyber policy to fill the gap.

findings.requirement_type: Tech E&O — Split Limits Reduce Coverage on Pre-2021 Wrongful Acts
findings.gap_description: The Gemini Tech E&O primary appears on the Dec page as $5M/$5M with retro 03/27/2017 — but Endorsement #4 carves the limits into three tiers based on when the Wrongful Act first commenced. Wrongful Acts dating between 12/1/2007 and 09/05/2019 are limited to $1M/$1M; acts between 09/06/2019 and 03/31/2021 carry an additional $1M xs $1M; only acts on or after 04/01/2021 enjoy the full $5M/$5M tower. Combined with the $5M Convex excess (which follows form and inherits the same split structure), only post-04/01/2021 wrongful acts have access to the full $10M tower. For a 50+ year-old election services company, claims arising from earlier Wrongful Acts (pre-2021 ballot processing engagements that surface in litigation later) face a $1M coverage cap. The Hanover Umbrella expressly excludes Professional Liability (475-0031), so umbrella drop-down is unavailable. Sacramento §III.E minimum of $1M/$1M is technically met for any tier — but the structural shortcoming is real.

findings.requirement_type: D&O — Prior Acts Cutoff 8/18/2023 (PE-Backed Risk)
findings.gap_description: The Hartford Management Liability policy bars coverage for any claim arising from Wrongful Acts prior to 08/18/2023 — meaning only ~1 year of prior-acts protection on policy effective 08/18/2024. For a 50+ year-old PE-backed company, this is dangerously narrow. Pre-2023 D&O exposures (governance decisions, financial misstatements, employment matters, regulatory compliance issues from prior years) are wholly uninsured. PE-backed companies are particularly exposed because the PE acquisition itself can be the basis for later litigation (purchase-price disputes, valuation challenges, prior-period accounting issues). Combined with the split Prior or Pending Date on the upper $1M D&O layer (4/2/2024), the program has structural holes. No other D&O policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Crime — Social Engineering / Deception Fraud Sublimited to $15K
findings.covered_by_which_policy: AmTrust Cyber Deception ($250K limit / $250K retention phantom — finding-003); combined effective coverage still $0-$250K
findings.gap_description: The Hartford Crime form provides only $15,000 of Deception Fraud (social engineering) coverage. Combined with the AmTrust Cyber Deception phantom coverage (finding-003), the program offers effectively no protection against fraudulent-instruction wire transfer fraud. Run-Test processes county invoices, vendor payables, and inter-company transfers — typical attack vectors for impersonation/spoofing fraud. Industry loss data shows social engineering attacks averaging $130K-$500K per incident, with the largest exceeding $10M. $15K is a token amount.

findings.requirement_type: GL — Sacramento 'No Additional Exclusions' vs Hanover GL Cyber/Privacy Stack
findings.covered_by_which_policy: AmTrust Cyber covers privacy/network security claims, but with limit and structural gaps per findings 1-9
findings.gap_description: Sacramento §II.A requires CG 00 01 'without additional exclusions or limitations, unless approved by the County Risk Manager.' The Hanover Package GL carries 11+ restrictive endorsements including three overlapping cyber/privacy exclusions (421-5286, CG 00 69, CG 21 06). In practice, county Risk Managers routinely accept these standard exclusions on COIs from manufacturers — but the contract technically requires written Risk Manager approval. The cyber/privacy exclusions are particularly relevant given Sacramento Voter Registration System work — a future privacy claim would be barred under GL and would need to fall under Cyber.

findings.requirement_type: Inland Marine — Waiver of Subrogation (Sacramento)
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Hanover Package Property — but only $100K BPP in transit and no WoS
findings.gap_description: Sacramento §IX requires WoS on any Inland Marine policy. Run-Test Election Services operates ballot scanners, sorters, printers, and election technology equipment that is regularly transported between facilities and county sites — classic Inland Marine exposure. The Hanover Package Property limits ($21.3M building, $16.3M BPP) suggest substantial equipment value, but only $100K of in-transit coverage is provided via the broadening endorsement. There appears to be no dedicated Inland Marine / Motor Truck Cargo / Equipment Floater policy. If equipment is damaged in transit while serving Sacramento, the $100K extension is likely inadequate, AND no WoS is in place. The contractual requirement is conditional ('Any Inland Marine insurance policies maintained by the CONTRACTOR') — so technically if no IM is maintained, there's nothing to endorse — but the underlying property-in-transit exposure is a real coverage gap.

findings.requirement_type: Carrier Rating Verification — Surplus Lines Carriers
findings.policy_file: Redacted2025 - 2026 Professional Liability Policy.pdf; RedactedConvex - 2025-2026 Excess Tech EO Policy.pdf; RedactedCyber_Assoc Industries.AmTrust_04.25-04.26 #AES123191302.pdf
findings.gap_description: Three program carriers are surplus lines / non-admitted: Gemini, Convex (UK), and AmTrust/Associated Industries. AM Best ratings have not been confirmed in the analysis. Sacramento requires A-VII minimum (more demanding than Maricopa's B++). Need to verify: Gemini (W.R. Berkley group typically A+ XV — likely OK); Convex Insurance UK Limited (UK-regulated subsidiary; AM Best rating may differ from US-rated carriers); AmTrust/Associated Industries (typically A- XII — likely OK for Maricopa, may meet Sacramento). Note: per KB Rule 15, surplus lines placement on Tech E&O and Cyber is appropriate — these markets are routinely placed E&S and this is not a critical finding by itself. Concern is rating verification only.

findings.requirement_type: Cyber — Proof of Loss Sublimit $250K
findings.gap_description: AmTrust Cyber Proof of Loss sublimit is $250,000. To prove up a multi-million-dollar Business Interruption claim against the $4M shared aggregate, forensic accountants typically charge $500K-$1.5M. The sublimit caps recoverable forensic accounting expenses at $200K (after retention). Insufficient to support a complex BI claim on a multi-county election services operation. No other cyber policy to fill the gap.

findings.requirement_type: Workers' Compensation — Multi-State Statutory Coverage Including California
findings.gap_description: Hanover (Massachusetts Bay) WC policy expressly schedules California as a covered state under Part 3.A and includes California-specific Broad Form Endorsement WC 99 03 04 03 16. Arizona is also expressly scheduled. Other States Insurance covers any non-monopolistic state not listed in 3.A. Multi-state coverage is robust for an AZ-based vendor operating in 31 states.

findings.requirement_type: Workers' Compensation — Blanket Waiver of Subrogation (Including California)
findings.gap_description: Two waiver of subrogation endorsements are in place: WC 00 03 13 blanket-by-contract for 9 states, and WC 04 03 06 California-specific blanket. Both Sacramento (California work) and Maricopa (Arizona work) requirements are satisfied. Premium is being charged ($50-$250 per state, plus 2% of CA WC premium) — reflects active waiver placement, not phantom coverage.

findings.requirement_type: Employer's Liability — Limits Meet Both Contracts
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Hanover Umbrella Coverage A — follows form over EL adding $10M
findings.gap_description: EL limits are $1M / $1M / $1M, meeting both Sacramento (single $1M minimum) and Maricopa ($1M/$1M/$1M) requirements. Hanover Umbrella Coverage A also follows form over EL via the Schedule of Underlying.

findings.requirement_type: GL — Additional Insured Ongoing + Completed Operations (Blanket-by-Contract)
findings.policy_file: RedactedHanover - Commercial - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf; Redacted2025-2026 Liability Policy - Security Guards.pdf
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Arch Security Guards GL also has blanket ongoing + completed ops AI but is scoped to security operations only
findings.gap_description: The Hanover Package GL includes 421-2915 Broadening Endorsement which provides blanket-by-contract AI status for ongoing operations. The Arch Security Guards GL has CG 20 10 + CG 20 37 (ongoing AND completed operations). Verify which policy is intended to respond to county contracts — the Arch policy is dedicated to security operations only and may NOT extend to election services activities. The Hanover Package GL is the operative policy for general election services. Hanover does NOT clearly schedule a completed operations AI endorsement (the broadening endorsement language at 421-2915 §1.c covers 'your work for the additional insured' which can include completed ops, but explicit CG 20 37 is preferred). Sacramento §VII.A requires AI 'as respects products and completed operations.' Recommend confirming.

findings.requirement_type: GL — Primary & Noncontributory + Waiver of Subrogation (Blanket)
findings.gap_description: Hanover Package GL includes blanket Primary & Non-Contributory and blanket Waiver of Subrogation, both triggered by written contract. CG 24 04 standalone WoS form provides additional belt-and-suspenders protection across both ongoing and completed operations. Both Sacramento §VII.C and Maricopa §8.2.4/§8.2.8 P&NC and WoS requirements are satisfied for GL. Note: Sacramento does NOT require GL WoS (§VII excludes WoS from GL list — only WC, COC, and IM). Maricopa requires WoS on GL — satisfied.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Additional Insured + P&NC + Waiver of Subrogation (Blanket)
findings.gap_description: Hanover Auto includes blanket Additional Insured (461-0478) with P&NC built in, PLUS blanket Waiver of Subrogation (461-0500), PLUS Broadening Endorsement Item 18 reinforcing WoS. All three contractually-required Auto provisions (AI, P&NC, WoS) are satisfied via blanket-by-contract trigger. Also note: Symbol 1 'any auto' coverage on liability is in place; hired auto cost-of-hire and non-owned (55 employees) are scheduled.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Hired & Non-Owned + Owned Coverage
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Hanover Umbrella adds $9M xs $1M to satisfy Maricopa $2M CSL minimum
findings.gap_description: Hanover Auto provides liability for owned, hired, and non-owned autos via the standard Business Auto Coverage Form CA 00 01 03 06 (the exact form Sacramento §II.B mandates). Maricopa $2M CSL is met by stacking $1M Auto + $9M Umbrella. Sacramento $1M CSL met directly. HNOA properly scheduled.

findings.requirement_type: Tech E&O — $10M Tower Far Exceeds $1M Sacramento Minimum
findings.policy_file: Redacted2025 - 2026 Professional Liability Policy.pdf; RedactedConvex - 2025-2026 Excess Tech EO Policy.pdf
findings.gap_description: Sacramento §III.E requires $1M/$1M Professional Liability minimum. Maricopa contract is silent on a specific E&O minimum. The Run-Test program carries $10M total Tech E&O — 10x the Sacramento minimum. Coverage is appropriately scoped via End. #9 (VP 02 75 07 17) which defines Professional Services to include 'Election ballot services, printing ballot services, election printing, petition printing and services, election and petition design, ballot fulfillment, election hardware and software maintenance, support and technical services, outbound and inbound mail processing services, and election & petition products and services' — directly aligned with Run-Test's actual operations. Subject to Split Limits caveat in finding-010 for pre-2021 acts.

findings.requirement_type: Tech E&O — Retroactive Date 03/27/2017 Predates Active Contracts
findings.policy_file: Redacted2025 - 2026 Professional Liability Policy.pdf; RedactedConvex - 2025-2026 Excess Tech EO Policy.pdf
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Convex Excess Tech E&O — matching 03/27/2017 retro
findings.gap_description: Both Gemini primary and Convex excess have matching Retroactive Dates of 03/27/2017. This precedes any reasonable contract effective date for Sacramento (which requires retro on/before contract date) and Maricopa (which requires retro PRECEDES contract effective). Tech E&O retro coverage extends back nearly 9 years on the broad-tier (post-04/01/2021) layer. Subject to Split Limits structure caveat in finding-010 — earlier-tier acts (pre-2021) only get $1M of coverage.

findings.requirement_type: Umbrella — $10M Stacks Over GL/Auto/EL to Meet Maricopa $2M Auto and $4M GL Aggregate
findings.policy_page: Umbrella Dec / Schedule of Underlying p 14
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Convex Excess Tech E&O fills the umbrella's professional liability exclusion gap
findings.gap_description: Hanover Umbrella $10M follows form over GL ($1M/$2M), Auto ($1M CSL), EL ($1M/$1M/$1M), and EBL ($1M/$1M). Stacking analysis: GL $1M + $10M umbrella = $11M each occurrence (meets Maricopa $2M); GL $2M agg + $10M umbrella products/comp ops agg = $12M (meets Maricopa $4M). Auto $1M + $10M umbrella = $11M (meets Maricopa $2M). EL $1M + $10M = $11M. Maricopa §8.2.9 expressly permits this stacking. Sacramento §II.E permits umbrella over GL/Auto/EL/EBL but EXPRESSLY EXCLUDES Professional Liability — Tech E&O cannot be supplemented by this umbrella, but the dedicated Convex Excess Tech E&O addresses that. NOTE: Umbrella DOES NOT follow form over Cyber (475-0654/0655/0661) — Cyber must satisfy Maricopa $5M alone.

findings.requirement_type: California Civil Code §2782(b) Anti-Indemnity Compliance
findings.policy_file: Redacted2025-2026 Liability Policy - Security Guards.pdf; RedactedHanover - Commercial - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf
findings.gap_description: California Civil Code §2782(b) bars contractor indemnity for the active (sole) negligence of the indemnitee. This is automatically built into the ISO 'insured contract' definition (CG 00 01 04 13 §V.9.f) which excludes 'that part of any contract or agreement that pertains to the rental of motor vehicles to you or any of your employees by the lessor' and limits insured-contract assumed liability to tort liability of another party. The Arch GL 00 GL1058 endorsement explicitly carves out sole negligence indemnity from insured contract. Compliance with Sacramento §VII.B is structural to the policy form.

findings.requirement_type: First Named Insured — Inc vs LLC Entity-Type Mismatch Across Program (Systemic)
findings.contract_quote: Insurance is to be placed with insurers with a current A.M. Best's rating of A-VII or better and shall be of the type and character listed... CONTRACTOR shall furnish the COUNTY with original endorsements effecting coverage required by these specifications.
findings.contract_file: RedactedAppendix G - Sacramento County Minimum Insurance Requirements.pdf; Redactedscrubbed - Maricopa Contract.pdf
findings.policy_quote: First Named Insured = 'Runbeck Election Services Inc' on Hanover WC, Hanover Auto, Hanover Commercial Package, Hanover Commercial Umbrella, and Gemini Professional Liability. First Named Insured = 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC' on Hartford Management Liability, Arch Security Guards CGL, Convex Excess Tech E&O, and AmTrust Cyber. AmTrust Cyber Policy Change #1 (IL 12 01 11 85) effective 4/1/2025 corrected the name to LLC — same correction was NOT propagated to the other 8 policies.
findings.policy_page: WC Dec; Auto Dec; Package Dec; Umbrella Dec; Pro Liab Dec; ML Dec; Arch CGL Dec; Convex Dec; AmTrust Cyber Policy Change #1 p 2
findings.gap_description: Five of nine program policies (all Hanover policies plus Gemini Pro Liab) name 'Runbeck Election Services Inc' as First Named Insured. Four policies — including the Cyber, which received a corrective endorsement on 4/1/2025 — name the LLC. This is a systemic identification defect: in any litigation, the party named on the Hanover policies is technically a different legal person than the party named on the ML/Cyber/E&O/Arch policies. The fact that ONE policy was corrected mid-term but the other eight were not is evidence the issue was identified for one policy and never propagated. Carriers can deny coverage on grounds of 'no insurable interest' if the named legal entity does not actually exist or differs from the entity that signed the contract or suffered the loss. For PE-backed companies in the middle of acquisitions or post-close cleanup, this is the most common documentary defect that surfaces in claim litigation.
findings.plain_english: Six of your policies name 'Runbeck Election Services Inc' as the insured. Four others name 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC.' If your actual legal entity is the LLC (which the AmTrust correction in April 2025 strongly suggests), then six insurance policies are technically issued to a company that doesn't exist. The carrier can use that mismatch to delay or deny a claim on the grounds that 'the named insured is not the entity that suffered the loss.' This is fixable in 30 days with a policy change endorsement on each carrier — but it must be done before a claim, not after.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the true legal entity (Articles of Incorporation/Organization, Tax ID, AZ Corporation Commission filing). If the parent is in fact 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC,' issue a Name Change endorsement (IL 12 01 or carrier equivalent) on all six 'Inc' policies — Hanover WC, Hanover Auto, Hanover Commercial Package, Hanover Commercial Umbrella, Gemini Pro Liab, and any others — to align with the LLC entity-type. Verify Form-of-Business field reads 'Limited Liability Company' on each Dec page. Confirm Broad Form Named Insured endorsement (Hanover form 421-2916) does not exclude LLCs from automatic subsidiary coverage.
discoveryQuestions: Has Runbeck Election Services ever converted from a corporation to an LLC, or vice versa? If so, when, and was the broker notified at the time?
When the AmTrust Cyber name was corrected to LLC on 4/1/2025, did your broker review the rest of the program for the same defect, or was that change handled in isolation?

Does your customer-facing certificate of insurance show 'Inc' or 'LLC' to county procurement officers, and have any contract administrators ever flagged the entity name as inconsistent with the signing party?

If a $5M cyber claim were tendered tomorrow under AmTrust ('LLC') and a $5M premises claim under Hanover ('Inc'), would your defense counsel be defending the same legal person — or two different ones?

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Policy Named Insured — Lincoln Shields LLC Missing from Umbrella, Package CGL, and ML
findings.contract_quote: GENERAL LIABILITY: ... Including, but not limited to Premises/Operations, Products/Completed Operations, Contractual, and Personal & Advertising Injury, without additional exclusions or limitations... Each Occurrence: $1,000,000... ADDITIONAL INSURED STATUS: The COUNTY... are to be endorsed as additional insureds as respects: liability arising out of activities performed by or on behalf of the CONTRACTOR.
findings.contract_file: RedactedAppendix G - Sacramento County Minimum Insurance Requirements.pdf; Redactedscrubbed - Maricopa Contract.pdf
findings.policy_quote: Lincoln Shields LLC is listed as Additional Named Insured on Hanover Auto endorsement 461-0174 (p 28) and as Additional Insured on Gemini Professional Liability AD 66 16 04 09 End. #7 (p 27). Lincoln Shields LLC is NOT listed on the Hanover Commercial Umbrella 475-0174 schedule (p 56), is NOT listed on the Hanover Commercial Package, is NOT listed on the Hartford Management Liability, is NOT listed on the AmTrust Cyber, and is NOT listed on the Convex Excess Tech E&O.
findings.policy_page: Auto p 28; Pro Liab p 27; missing from Umbrella p 56; missing from Package p 12; missing from all others
findings.policy_file: RedactedHanover - Commercial Umbrella - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf; RedactedHanover - Commercial - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf; Redacted2024-26 Management Liability Policy.pdf
findings.gap_description: Lincoln Shields LLC is a subsidiary the broker chose to schedule onto the Auto and Pro Liab policies, evidencing it is a real Runbeck-family entity with operations and exposures. The Auto policy carries $1,000,000 CSL primary. The Hanover Umbrella schedule of named insureds (475-0174) does not include Lincoln Shields LLC. Any auto liability claim against Lincoln Shields exceeding $1M is uninsured — there is no Umbrella to drop down to because the Umbrella does not recognize Lincoln Shields as a Named Insured. Worse, Lincoln Shields is also absent from the Hanover Commercial Package CGL (p 12 schedule shows only Runbeck Election Services Inc, Runbeck Investments LLC, and Runbeck Graphics Inc.) — meaning a slip-and-fall, premises, or completed-operations claim against Lincoln Shields has zero CGL coverage in the program. And there is no Management Liability D&O coverage for any director or officer of Lincoln Shields. This is the GAP-20 flagship pattern: an entity is named on lower-tier primaries but missing from program excess and from sister primaries.
findings.plain_english: You insured a subsidiary called Lincoln Shields LLC on your auto policy and your professional liability policy — but you forgot it on your umbrella, your general liability policy, and your D&O. Translation: if a Lincoln Shields vehicle hits a school bus, you have $1M of coverage and zero excess. If a visitor slips and falls at any Lincoln Shields location, there is no general liability coverage at all — anywhere in the program. If the Lincoln Shields directors get sued, no D&O responds. This subsidiary is exposed at the umbrella attachment point and on premises liability at any limit.
findings.recommendation: Add Lincoln Shields LLC to Hanover Umbrella schedule (475-0174) by endorsement. Add Lincoln Shields LLC to Hanover Commercial Package Schedule of Named Insureds. Add Lincoln Shields LLC to the Hartford Management Liability Schedule of Subsidiaries. Confirm the auto and pro-liab schedules already in place do not need to be re-papered after the umbrella correction.
discoveryQuestions: What does Lincoln Shields LLC actually do — is it an operating subsidiary, a property-holding entity, a leasing entity, or something else? The answer drives which coverages need to be on which policies.
Does Lincoln Shields LLC own or lease any premises, employ any people, or operate any vehicles? If yes to any of these, the gap is real and current.

If a customer contract requires the contracting entity to be insured for $10M and you certified using the umbrella, does Lincoln Shields appear as the contracting entity anywhere in your customer agreements?
When Lincoln Shields LLC was added to the auto policy, was a coordinated request made to update every other policy in the program, or was the request limited to auto?

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Policy Named Insured — Black Mountain Investment Co. LLC Missing from Umbrella, Package CGL, and ML
findings.contract_quote: Insurance shall be obtained from insurance companies licensed and authorized to do business... CONTRACTOR shall furnish the COUNTY with original endorsements effecting coverage required by these specifications.
findings.contract_file: RedactedAppendix G - Sacramento County Minimum Insurance Requirements.pdf
findings.policy_quote: Black Mountain Investment Co. LLC is listed as Additional Named Insured on Hanover Auto endorsement 461-0174 (p 28). It also appears on the Gemini Professional Liability under the slightly variant name 'Black Mountain Investment Company LLC' on AD 66 16 04 09 End. #7 (p 27). Black Mountain is NOT listed on the Hanover Commercial Umbrella 475-0174, NOT on the Hanover Commercial Package, NOT on the Hartford Management Liability, NOT on the AmTrust Cyber, NOT on the Convex Excess.

findings.policy_quote: Runbeck Properties, LLC IS listed on the Hanover Commercial Umbrella 475-0174 schedule (p 56), IS listed on the Hanover Auto 461-0174 schedule (p 28), and IS listed on the AmTrust Cyber after Policy Change #1 (p 2). Runbeck Properties, LLC is NOT listed on the Hanover Commercial Package CGL — Schedule of Named Insureds (p 12) only shows Runbeck Election Services Inc, Runbeck Investments LLC, and Runbeck Graphics Inc.
findings.policy_page: Hanover Commercial Package Schedule of Named Insureds p 12 — Runbeck Properties, LLC absent. Umbrella p 56 — present.
findings.gap_description: This is the most severe pattern in the GAP-20 framework: an entity is named on the Umbrella but is NOT named on the underlying Primary CGL. The Umbrella is structured as Excess Liability and Umbrella Liability that requires underlying coverage to follow form to. If a premises liability claim occurs at a Runbeck Properties, LLC location, the Hanover Commercial Package CGL does not respond at all because Runbeck Properties is not a Named Insured on that policy. The Umbrella then has nothing to drop down over — there is no underlying claim payment to attach excess to, and umbrellas typically do not drop down to fill a gap where the named insured was simply omitted from the primary. This is functionally an uninsured exposure across the entire program for premises claims at Runbeck Properties locations. Runbeck Properties is the entity that, by name, almost certainly holds the real estate. Real estate is the highest-frequency premises liability exposure in the program.
findings.plain_english: This is the worst kind of gap. Runbeck Properties LLC — which by its name is your real-estate-holding entity — is listed on your $10M umbrella and on your auto policy, but somebody forgot to put it on your underlying general liability policy. So a slip-and-fall, a stairway injury, an HVAC accident at any Runbeck Properties building has zero coverage. The umbrella can't help you because there's no primary policy underneath for it to follow. Your $10M umbrella schedule doesn't matter when the primary doesn't recognize the entity. This is fixable for free with an endorsement, and it must be done immediately.
findings.recommendation: Issue an immediate endorsement to the Hanover Commercial Package adding 'Runbeck Properties, LLC' to the Schedule of Named Insureds (currently page 12). Verify the addition flows through to the products/completed-operations aggregate and the per-project aggregate. Confirm the Hanover Broad Form Named Insured endorsement (421-2916) does not exclude LLCs from automatic coverage; if it does, the express schedule addition is required (which it is here regardless).
discoveryQuestions: Which Runbeck buildings — manufacturing, headquarters, warehouse, ballot processing centers — are owned or held by Runbeck Properties, LLC versus by an operating entity?

If a county election worker came on-site to do printing acceptance testing and was injured at a Runbeck Properties building, who would the customer's lawyer name as the defendant — the operating entity, the property owner, or both?

Has the PE sponsor required real estate to be held in a separate LLC for asset-protection or financing reasons? If so, did that financing structure assume the real-estate entity would carry GL/property in its own name?
When Runbeck Properties was added to the umbrella schedule (475-0174), was the underlying CGL policy reviewed to make sure the entity was added there too, or was that step missed?

findings.requirement_type: Fiduciary Liability — Runbeck Companies 401(k) Profit Sharing Plan Not Listed as Named Insured on ML Policy
findings.contract_quote: Customer contracts (Maricopa, Sacramento, Los Angeles, Douglas County) do not directly reference 401(k) plan coverage. ERISA §404 imposes fiduciary obligations on plan sponsors and trustees independently of any customer contract; Fiduciary Liability coverage exists to protect plan sponsors against participant-driven claims for breach of fiduciary duty in plan administration, investment selection, and fee reasonableness.
findings.policy_quote: 'Runbeck Companies 401(k) Profit Sharing Plan' is listed as Additional Named Insured on Hanover Auto 461-0174 (p 28) — a policy that has no fiduciary relevance. The plan is NOT listed as a Named Insured on the Hartford Management Liability Policy Fiduciary Coverage Part schedule. The Fiduciary aggregate on the ML policy is $1,000,000 with $0 retention, but the policy must list the Plan to extend coverage to the Plan's own claims.
findings.policy_page: Auto p 28 (irrelevant scheduling); ML Fiduciary Coverage Part — Plan not scheduled
findings.gap_description: The Runbeck Companies 401(k) Profit Sharing Plan is scheduled as an Additional Named Insured on the Auto policy — which makes no sense (a 401(k) plan doesn't drive vehicles). It is NOT scheduled on the Management Liability Fiduciary Coverage Part — which is exactly where it belongs. Fiduciary liability policies extend coverage to the Plan, the Plan Administrator, the Plan Trustees, and (sometimes) the plan sponsor's officers and directors in their fiduciary capacity. Without the Plan named, ERISA §502(a)(2) plan-restoration claims (where the plaintiff sues 'the Plan' directly) may not trigger Fiduciary coverage. PE-backed companies face heightened ERISA scrutiny because PE sponsors are increasingly named in fee-litigation suits where plaintiffs argue the sponsor breached fiduciary duties by negotiating sub-optimal recordkeeping fees with affiliated providers.
findings.plain_english: Your 401(k) plan is somehow listed as an additional insured on the auto policy — which is nonsensical, plans don't drive cars. The place it actually needs to be listed is on the Fiduciary Coverage Part of your Management Liability policy. If a plan participant sues the plan or its trustees over a fee dispute or investment loss, the carrier may take the position that the Plan itself is not a named insured under fiduciary coverage and decline to defend. This is a one-endorsement fix but has serious ERISA-class-action implications, especially under a PE-backed ownership structure where fee-litigation plaintiffs love to drag the sponsor in.
findings.recommendation: (1) Schedule 'Runbeck Companies 401(k) Profit Sharing Plan' as a Named Insured on the Hartford Management Liability Fiduciary Coverage Part. (2) Remove the Plan from the Auto Multiple Named Insured schedule — it is improperly placed and creates confusion. (3) Confirm Fiduciary Coverage Part definition of 'Insured' captures plan trustees, plan administrators, and individuals serving as fiduciaries. (4) Verify whether the policy includes a Settlor Functions exclusion that may bar coverage for plan-design decisions made by the sponsor.
discoveryQuestions: Who serves as the named fiduciaries on the 401(k) plan — is it Runbeck officers, an outside committee, or a third-party trustee like Mercer or Empower?
Has the PE sponsor or its operating partners taken any role in selecting or reviewing the 401(k) recordkeeper, advisor, or investment menu? If yes, that creates direct fiduciary exposure.
Have any plan participants raised concerns about fees, investment options, or plan administration in the last 12 months, formally or informally?
Is there a Plan Document committee charter that names individuals acting in a fiduciary capacity — and are those named individuals Insured Persons under the ML policy?

(the printing/graphics operating sister) — are scheduled across the property, casualty, cyber, and excess policies but are NOT on the Hartford Management Liability schedule of subsidiaries. The Hartford ML form may have automatic subsidiary coverage if the entities meet the policy's definition of 'Subsidiary' (typically >50% direct or indirect ownership), but Hartford Private Choice Premier policies often require entities to be specifically scheduled if they are LLCs (the same Broad Form NI exclusion pattern that affects GL extensions). findings.plain_english: Two of your operating companies — Runbeck Investments LLC and Runbeck Graphics Inc. — appear on every policy in your program except the one that protects your directors and officers. If a Graphics customer or contracting party sues the Graphics directors for breach of fiduciary duty or an investigation hits Runbeck Investments, your D&O carrier may say 'this entity isn't on the schedule, we don't owe defense.' The entire point of D&O on a multi-entity holding structure is to capture every operating subsidiary on the schedule, because that's where the actual operating risk lives.
findings.recommendation: Request a no-cost or modest-premium endorsement scheduling Runbeck Investments LLC, Runbeck Graphics Inc., Runbeck Properties LLC, Lincoln Shields LLC, and Black Mountain Investment Co. LLC as Subsidiaries on the Hartford Management Liability Policy. discoveryQuestions: How is the corporate hierarchy structured — is Runbeck Investments LLC the holding company that owns the operating entities, or a sister entity for tax structuring?
Does Runbeck Graphics Inc. have its own board of directors or officers separate from Runbeck Election Services, and have they ever faced a regulatory inquiry, customer dispute, or vendor lawsuit?
When the PE sponsor closed on Runbeck, was there a roll-up of subsidiaries or a re-org that created or eliminated entities — and was the ML policy updated to reflect the post-close structure?

findings.gap_description: The landlord ARC Airport 2800, LLC is correctly added as Additional Insured on the primary CGL via CG 20 18 04 13 (Lessor of Leased Equipment / Manager of Real Estate, depending on form variant). However, commercial leases routinely require the tenant to extend AI status to the landlord 'on a primary and noncontributory basis up to the full limits of all insurance maintained by Tenant,' which includes the umbrella. The Umbrella schedule does not list ARC Airport. If a tenant-related premises liability claim against the landlord exceeds the $1M CGL primary, the umbrella may not extend to the landlord because (a) the umbrella is not a true follow-form for AI status without express scheduling, and (b) the landlord is not named on the umbrella schedule of insureds.
findings.plain_english: Your landlord — ARC Airport 2800 LLC — is added to your general liability policy as required by the lease, but they're not on your $10M umbrella. Most commercial leases require landlord coverage 'up to the full limits of all insurance,' which means your umbrella too. If a really bad slip-and-fall judgment exceeds your $1M GL primary, the landlord's recovery against your insurance may stop at $1M and the landlord will tender to you personally for the excess — which the lease's indemnification clause requires you to cover.

The Hanover NOC endorsements 401-1235 and 331-0342 evidence that Boulder, San Luis Obispo, El Paso, Coconino, State of Colorado, NY State OGS, and Amazon are contractually entitled to such notice on at least one program policy.

Hanover WC 331-0342 (p 112) lists: El Paso County, Coconino County, Amazon.com. Hanover Commercial Package 401-1235 (p 36) lists ONLY: NY State OGS, Amazon, ARC Airport 2800, Banterra Bank. findings.policy_page: Auto pp 44-46; WC p 112; Package p 36 — asymmetric customer schedules
findings.gap_description: The fact that the Hanover Auto policy lists eight customer entities (plus blanket-by-contract) on the Designated Entity NOC schedule is presumptive evidence those customer contracts require NOC. The same customers almost universally require NOC on CGL too — this is the GAP-21 asymmetry. The Hanover Commercial Package CGL NOC schedule is materially shorter than the Auto schedule, and it adds two entities (ARC Airport, Banterra Bank) that are landlord/lender, not customer counties. Specific customer entities present on Auto but missing from the Package CGL: City of Boulder, San Luis Obispo County, State of Colorado, El Paso County, Coconino County. WC includes only El Paso, Coconino, Amazon — missing the rest. This means the Package CGL can be cancelled tomorrow without notice to Boulder, SLO, Colorado, El Paso, or Coconino, even though the Auto policy would be required to send them notice. Customers in those counties may treat this as an uncured contract breach; in worst case, they could terminate the contract or apply liquidated damages.
findings.plain_english: When you cancel or non-renew an insurance policy, your customers expect their procurement office to get a heads-up letter. Five of your customer counties (Boulder, San Luis Obispo, Colorado state, El Paso, Coconino) are on your auto policy's notice list but are completely missing from your general liability policy's notice list. If your GL policy got cancelled mid-term, those five customers would not be notified — even though their contracts almost certainly require it. This is the kind of administrative breach a procurement officer can use to terminate or assess penalties, even if no actual claim is involved.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the NOC schedules across all three Hanover policies (Auto, WC, Package CGL). Identify every customer counterparty whose contract requires NOC and ensure each entity appears on every applicable program policy with notice period at least equal to the contract requirement (typically 30 days, sometimes 60 or 90). Use the Auto policy's NOC schedule as the baseline — it's the most complete — and replicate to Package and WC where the customer relationship implicates that coverage line.
discoveryQuestions: Pull each county contract — Boulder, San Luis Obispo, El Paso, Coconino, Colorado state — and identify the exact insurance article. Do they require NOC on 'all required insurance' or only on specific lines?

If your Hanover Commercial Package CGL got non-renewed mid-cycle, would your customer service team know which county procurement offices to call manually, or are you relying on the carrier's NOC endorsement to do that work?
Have any of your customer counties ever asked for a 60-day or 90-day notice — and if so, is the 30-day notice on the Hanover endorsements actually adequate?

Customer contracts requiring NOC are typically not limited to a single coverage line; they apply to 'any required insurance' or 'all policies of insurance evidencing the coverages required herein.'

findings.policy_file: Redacted2024-26 Management Liability Policy.pdf; Redacted2025 - 2026 Professional Liability Policy.pdf; Redacted2025-2026 Liability Policy - Security Guards.pdf; RedactedConvex - 2025-2026 Excess Tech EO Policy.pdf; RedactedCyber_Assoc Industries.AmTrust_04.25-04.26 #AES123191302.pdf; RedactedHanover - Commercial Umbrella - 4.1.25-4.1.26.pdf
findings.gap_description: Six of nine program policies have no Designated Entity Notice of Cancellation endorsement at all. Customer contracts typically require NOC on 'all policies of insurance evidencing the coverages required herein,' which would include Cyber (Maricopa explicitly requires Cyber), the Umbrella (most contracts require Umbrella when it's used to satisfy primary minimums), and the Pro Liab/Tech E&O tower (election technology customers care deeply about E&O continuity). For coverage lines the customer contractually requires — Cyber for Maricopa, E&O for tech customers, Umbrella for any contract requiring $5M+ — the absence of NOC is a current contract-administration breach. The Umbrella absence is particularly meaningful because the Umbrella is the policy that satisfies higher-limit requirements, and customers entitled to NOC on the GL are entitled by extension to NOC on the policy that provides the bulk of the limit they paid for.
findings.plain_english: Your customer contracts require advance notice if any insurance gets cancelled. Hanover sets up that notice on three policies — auto, WC, and the package — but six other policies in your program have no notice mechanism at all. Your $4M cyber, your $10M umbrella, your $10M E&O tower, your D&O — none of them will tell your customers if they get cancelled. For a Maricopa-style contract that explicitly requires $5M cyber, the cyber policy disappearing without notice is a textbook contract breach.
findings.recommendation: For each customer contract, identify which coverage lines the contract enumerates as required. For each enumerated line, request the carrier add a Designated Entity NOC endorsement listing the customer counterparty with notice period ≥ contract requirement. Priority order: (1) AmTrust Cyber (Maricopa explicitly requires Cyber); (2) Hanover Umbrella (carries the limit that satisfies most contracts); (3) Gemini Pro Liab and Convex Excess (election-tech customers care about E&O continuity); (4) Hartford ML and Arch Security Guards CGL where customer contracts reach those lines.
discoveryQuestions: Has any customer ever asked Runbeck to provide proof of NOC endorsement on Cyber or Umbrella, and if so, how was the request handled?

If your AmTrust Cyber policy were cancelled mid-term tomorrow, what would your customer-success team do — call counties manually, or rely on the carrier to send notice (which they're not contractually obligated to do)?
When PE sponsors complete due diligence on Runbeck for follow-on financing, do they typically ask for evidence that customer NOC obligations are satisfied across all required policy lines?

So if a Lincoln Shields driver causes a $5M crash, you have $1M of coverage and a $4M problem. The umbrella's $10M is irrelevant because the umbrella doesn't recognize Lincoln Shields.
